plan.summary: This 4-week block starts the 12-week off-camp build for boxing with one weekly bodyweight-only session. Week 1 establishes simple baseline performance on the main lower-body strength pattern so later work can be progressed clearly, and the main training block starts in Week 2. Because boxing is off-camp and you want strength-power with a bit more conditioning, the plan keeps one quality strength-power session each week and finishes with short conditioning that supports the sport without creating unnecessary fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic lower-body strength, trunk stiffness, and explosive intent with simple bodyweight work and short conditioning.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress unilateral strength and explosive output while keeping the weekly workload recoverable around boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength topped up and shift more of the session toward crisp speed, jumps, and sharp conditioning.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can with a quick dip and a quiet landing. Rest fully between sets and stop if height drops off.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if space is tight. Start from a still quarter squat and drive straight up.

substitutionOptions.name: Low Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low safe box if landing mechanics are better with a target.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a controlled tempo and stop when depth or balance breaks. This establishes your baseline for future progression on the main strength pattern.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up with easy bodyweight reps, then perform one hard set per side for as many clean reps as possible in the 5-15 rep range. Log reps for each side so the app can set your starting progression.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean rep count per side with full depth and steady balance.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rear-foot elevation irritates your hips, knees, or balance.

substitutionOptions.name: Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a stable box or bench if split squat setup is awkward.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Leave 1-2 good reps in reserve. Keep ribs down, body straight, and lower under control.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a bench, table, or bar if full push-ups are not yet clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Knee Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a simpler option and keep the torso braced.

exercises.name: Towel Row
exercises.notes: Use a sturdy anchor and pull elbows back without shrugging. Make each rep smooth and controlled.

substitutionOptions.name: Inverted Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a stable bar or rings if available.

substitutionOptions.name: Backpack Bent-Over Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a loaded backpack if a safe row anchor is not available.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Press the low back into the floor and keep the position tight. Shorten the lever if you cannot hold shape.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the full hollow hold is too difficult to keep clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Crunch
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a dynamic trunk option instead of a hold.

exercises.name: Alternating Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Move smoothly and keep the front foot flat. This is extra leg volume, not a max-effort drill.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if stepping back bothers your balance.

substitutionOptions.name: Bodyweight Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low stable box if lunges are uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Conditioning Finisher
exercises.notes: 6 rounds of 20 seconds fast shadowboxing and 40 seconds easy movement. Keep punches crisp and relaxed, and finish feeling worked but not cooked.
